headline: Protein models are probed for evolutionary signal, structural bias, and design utility
label: Protein Models And Evolutionary Structure
summary: New work tests where AlphaFold and protein language models succeed or fail on non-globular proteins, organism-level signal, and peptide design.
synthesis: The common thread is evaluating what learned protein models encode and where they fail, spanning evolutionary analysis, structure prediction and design. A Nature Methods review frames transformer foundation models for residue dependencies, pathogenicity and alignment-free evolutionary analysis. A PLOS Computational Biology analysis of 373,779 AlphaFold structures finds organism-specific physicochemical signatures that recover tree-of-life features, suggesting predicted structures carry phylogenetic information. A preprint on experimentally validated non-globular proteins shows AlphaFold predictions diverging from biologically relevant structural states. A generative model for peptides with custom secondary structure motifs and reduced amino acid alphabets is checked with ESMFold. What is new is the emphasis on bias, limits and latent content, not on accuracy alone.
